subject: Workplace Skills
title: The Currency of Reciprocity
description: A quick win: understand The Currency of Reciprocity.

hook.text: Robert Cialdini's research shows reciprocity is the strongest influence tool. People feel obligated to return favors.

buildup.text: In organizations, favors are currency: sharing information, lending team members, supporting someone's project.

discovery.text: Help others before you need their help. When you eventually ask, the reciprocity principle works in your favor.

twist.text: The favor doesn't need to match in size. A small, timely favor returned generously builds disproportionate influence.

climax.text: Look for opportunities to help cross-functional peers this week. Ask nothing in return yet. Build the credit.

punchline.text: Give first. Ask later. Reciprocity compounds quietly.

quiz.question: How does the reciprocity principle create influence?
options: People feel obligated to return favors, creating future leverage
Giving favors makes you popular and people agree with popular people
Reciprocity creates formal agreements between departments
